subject.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns

question: Should durable browser-tab cleanup retain unreachable rows indefinitely, or is a fixed 24-hour retirement window the intended user contract?
rationale: The code is mechanically bounded and tested, but choosing when persisted cleanup responsibility expires changes behavior for existing browser profiles and cannot be resolved from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Accept bounded retention
options.body: Approve the documented 24-hour unavailable-browser cutoff, then rebase and merge with the existing boundary coverage.

options.title: Preserve indefinite retry
options.body: Keep unreachable durable rows until ownership can be resolved, leaving the store-cap recovery problem for a separately approved design.

options.title: Choose a different policy
options.body: Specify a different retention duration or product surface before implementation proceeds.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded retention
recommendation.body: Approve the documented 24-hour unavailable-browser cutoff, then rebase and merge with the existing boundary coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: FMLS authored the merged durable-tab cleanup design whose ownership and cleanup guarantees are being narrowed by this follow-up.
